text: How do I break up with my girlfriend, even though I still love her? The guy is 22 years old male and the girl is 21 years old female. I love my girlfriend a lot. We haven't been dating too long, roughly six months. But since we started, we have had a very strong connection with each other. However, I just recently feel like we aren't compatible and neither of us can really meet each other's desires and needs in a relationship. It just sucks because over the past six months, we have had a lot of good times together and both of us would agree we love each other unconditionally. It's mostly just the intimacy that we are incompatible on. I don't want to just abandon her and honestly, I have too much self-respect to see myself continuing to settle with just friends. We've talked about it before and both of us have tried for each other, but usually the changes only last about a week before they kind of disappear and it's back to normal. All right, let's start with this. Don't be a drama queen. Sometimes the situation is simple, but guys love to dramatize it. Oh, what do I do? Please help me. Men, if you want to break up, just tell your girlfriend. Ideally, try to be ecological and considerate and say the classic line, it's not you, it's me. Done. Another thing. You're talking about how much you love each other unconditionally and how many good times you've had. Newsflash, every relationship has good moments. It's the bad ones that decide whether you should stay or leave. And you said it yourself, you are not compatible. That alone is enough. Now about the word love. Stop throwing it around in situations like this. If you two are not compatible, that's not love. Those are strong emotions, maybe attachment, maybe habit, but not love. Using the word love here really devalues its meaning. So here's the reality. You realize you are not compatible. You tried fixing it. It didn't work. It is important for a man to take responsibility and act. And learn to act yourself, not waiting until she will end it or situation will get much worse. Tell her straight, end it and move on. Nobody said it's easy, but being a man means you do what's necessary, even when it's hard.
